children: ), a leading global security products and solutions provider, today reported financial results for its third quarter (ended Sept. 30, 2026).

“I am pleased with our Q3 performance as we delivered high-single digit organic revenue growth and low teens adjusted EPS growth led by our Americas non-residential business,” Allegion President and CEO John H. Stone said.
“With steady momentum in our demand generation engine and a proven, resilient business model, we are raising our full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EPS outlook.”
(All comparisons are year-over-year, unless otherwise noted)

Allegion reported third-quarter 2026 net revenues of $1,172.6 million and net earnings of $220.9 million, or $2.59 per share. Adjusted net earnings were $221.0 million, or $2.60 per share, up 13.0%. (Details of the adjustments are included in the footnotes of the tables in this press release.)

Third-quarter 2026 net revenues increased 9.6%. On an organic basis, which excludes impacts of acquisitions, divestitures and foreign currency movements, net revenues increased 7.2%, led by the Americas region. The organic revenue increase was driven by volume growth and price realization. Reported revenue reflects a 2.6% net positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures, as well as a 0.2% headwind from foreign currency.

Third-quarter 2026 operating income was $284.6 million, an increase of $50.8 million or 21.7%. Adjusted operating income in third-quarter 2026 was $289.7 million, an increase of $32.3 million or 12.5%.

Third-quarter 2026 operating margin was 24.3%, compared with 21.8%. The adjusted operating margin in third-quarter 2026 was 24.7%, compared with 24.1%. The adjusted operating margin increase is attributable to favorable volume leverage as well as price and productivity net of inflation and investment (PPII), inclusive of transactional foreign currency, which was positive on a dollar basis and a tailwind to margin rate.
(All comparisons are year-over-year, unless otherwise noted)

The Americas segment revenues were up 11.7% (up 9.1% on an organic basis). The non-residential business was up low-double digits organically, driven by volume growth and price realization. The residential business was up mid-single digits organically, driven by price realization. The reported revenue reflects a 2.6% positive impact from acquisitions. Adjusted operating margin in the region increased 20 basis points to 30.1%. The adjusted operating margin increase is attributable to favorable volume leverage as well as PPII, inclusive of transactional foreign currency headwinds, which was positive on a dollar basis and a 20-basis point tailwind to margin rate. Acquisitions were a 40-basis point headwind to margin rate.

The International segment revenues were up 1.8% (down 0.2% on an organic basis). The slight organic revenue decrease was driven by volume declines, which more than offset favorable pricing. Reported revenue reflects a 2.5% net positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures and a 0.5% headwind from foreign currency. Adjusted operating margin in the region decreased 40 basis points to 13.9%, driven by volume declines and unfavorable mix offset partially by a PPII tailwind and favorable impacts from acquisitions.

Third-quarter 2026 reported results include the impact of IEEPA tariff refunds (tariff refunds), which benefited operating income by $19.9 million and interest income by $0.9 million. These benefits are excluded from adjusted operating income and adjusted EPS and reflect the impact from refunds received and expected to be received from the U.S. government.
(All comparisons are year-over-year, unless otherwise noted)
Interest expense for third-quarter 2026 was $24.2 million, a decrease of $2.4 million.

Other income, net for third-quarter 2026 was $7.4 million, compared to other income, net of $1.7 million. Other income, net for third-quarter 2026 includes a $4.1 million gain on non-operating investments and $0.9 million of interest income related to tariff refunds.
The company’s effective tax rate for third-quarter 2026 was 17.5%, compared with 9.8%. The company’s adjusted effective tax rate for third-quarter 2026 was 17.5%, compared with 14.9%.

Year-to-date available cash flow for 2026 was $539.4 million, an increase of $54.2 million versus the prior-year period. The company ended third-quarter 2026 with cash and cash equivalents of $388.1 million and total debt of $2,032.0 million.

In the third quarter of 2026, the company repurchased approximately 0.8 million shares for approximately $120 million and paid quarterly dividends of $0.55 per ordinary share or approximately $46 million.
(All comparisons are year-over-year, unless otherwise noted)

The company is raising its full-year 2026 reported revenue growth outlook to a range of 9.5% to 10.5% and is raising its organic growth outlook to a range of 5.0% to 6.0%, after excluding the expected impacts of acquisitions, divestitures and foreign currency movements.

The company is raising the outlook for full-year 2026 adjusted EPS to be in the range of $9.05 to $9.10. The company is updating the outlook for full-year 2026 reported EPS and expects it to be in the range of $8.35 to $8.40. Adjustments to 2026 EPS include estimated impacts of approximately $0.60 per share for acquisition-related amortization, $0.28 per share for restructuring, M&A and other adjustments as well as $0.18 per share benefit for tariff refunds.
The outlook continues to assume a full-year adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 18% to 19%.
The outlook assumes an average diluted share count for the full year of approximately 85.6 million shares.
The company continues to expect full-year available cash flow to be 85% to 95% of adjusted net income.

On Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, President and CEO John H. Stone and Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Mike Wagnes will conduct a conference call for analysts and investors, beginning at 8 a.m. ET, to review the company's results.
A real-time, listen-only webcast of the conference call will be broadcast live online. Individuals wishing to listen may access the call through https://investor.allegion.com.

The Company presents operating income, operating margin, earnings before income taxes, effective income tax rate, net earnings and diluted earnings per ordinary share (EPS) on both a U.S. GAAP basis and on an adjusted (non-GAAP) basis, revenue growth on a U.S. GAAP basis and organic revenue growth on a non-GAAP basis, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin (all non-GAAP measures), and available cash flow ("ACF", a non-GAAP measure). The Company presents these non-GAAP measures because management believes they provide useful perspective of the Company’s underlying business results and trends and a more comparable measure of period-over-period results. These measures are also used to evaluate senior management and are a factor in determining at-risk compensation. Investors should not consider non-GAAP measures as alternatives to the related U.S. GAAP measures.
The Company defines the presented non-GAAP measures as follows:

Adjustments to operating income, operating margin, earnings before income taxes, effective tax rate, net earnings, EPS and EBITDA include items such as goodwill, indefinite-lived trade name and other asset impairment charges, restructuring charges, acquisition and integration costs, amortization of acquired intangible assets, debt financing costs, gains or losses related to the divestiture of businesses or equity method investments, non-operating investment gains or losses, non-cash pension settlement charges, and tariff refunds;
Organic revenue growth is defined as U.S. GAAP revenue growth excluding the impact of acquisitions, divestitures and currency effects; and
ACF is defined as U.S. GAAP net cash from operating activities less capital expenditures.
These non-GAAP measures may not be defined and calculated the same as similar measures used by other companies.
